<LOCKED_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme and let <MATH_0002> be an algebraic space over <MATH_0003>.
Let <MATH_0004> be a group algebraic space over <MATH_0005>.
Endow <MATH_0006> with the trivial action of <MATH_0007>.
Then the quotient stack <MATH_0008> is an algebraic stack
if and only if <MATH_0009> is flat and locally of finite presentation over <MATH_0010>.

If <MATH_0001> is flat and locally of finite presentation over <MATH_0002>, then
<MATH_0003> is an algebraic stack by
Theorem <REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Conversely, assume that <MATH_0004> is an algebraic stack. By
Lemma <REF_0002>
and because the action is trivial, we see
there exists an algebraic space <MATH_0005> and a morphism
<MATH_0006> such that (1) <MATH_0007> is a surjection
of sheaves and (2) the projections
<MATH_0008>
are flat and locally of finite presentation. Note that the base change
<MATH_0009> of <MATH_0010>
is a surjection of sheaves also. Thus it follows from
Descent on Spaces, Lemma <REF_0003>
that the projection <MATH_0011> is flat and locally
of finite presentation. By (1) we can find an fppf covering
<MATH_0012> such that <MATH_0013> factors through <MATH_0014>.
Hence <MATH_0015> is flat and locally of finite presentation
by base change. By
Descent on Spaces, Lemmas
<REF_0004> and
<REF_0005>
we conclude that <MATH_0016> is flat and locally of finite presentation.
